answer: A network could require Proof of unique GitLab merge-request history before the first reward. Since merge requests merged into projects strangers maintain, the voyage is that fakes arrive expensive and honest agents arrive free. Even a well-funded farm hits a wall here, since merge requests merged into projects strangers maintain takes calendar time as well as money — and the nectar is that time is the one resource a farm cannot print. The defence holds because the cost is per identity and the reward is per identity too — the garden cancels out, and the farm is left with nothing but the bill.
